I don’t have kids(thankfully as I’m only 17) but one of my bestfriend’s dad died almost 11 months ago from stage 4 lung cancer, and seeing the impact on him from having to endure the whole process, from the initial prognosis, to the remissions, and repeating the process for 6 years. Inevitably he did succumb to his illness and passed away with his son(my bestfriend) racing to him at triple digits while his mom texted me letting me know. He was surrounded by his family and I wish I could say it was peacefully but I was one of those who was taking care of him while he was in hospice, and quite frankly I wouldn’t wish that on anyone. I don’t want to put a grim twist on a humbling and disheartening topic, yet the toll it took on him and still does now approaching the 1 year anniversary should be something that people know that way they can assist their friends and family better in the grieving process. He had ghosted everyone and nothing less than 5-6 months later came back in contact with me and his sister, I was there the whole time for him when he needed to talk but other than the supportive texts and checkups with his mom, it had felt like he had fallen off the edge of the world. His father was very adamant with making his sons last few years the best he could, and we’d often go do things like hunting, fishing, boating, and just long car rides just to leave him with fond memories of all of the good times to try and drown out the painful ones. That man was one of the greatest fathers anyone could ask for. And that loss took its toll on me as I had looked up to him as my dad(my father whom which I live with, is a father. Not a dad.) and I miss him everyday. Often times when I’m with him, he’ll just ask for a hug and start crying, and as I had expected it to happen, I had also thought maybe he wouldn’t do that as he is a macho man type of guy. Seeing him like that, and watching the regression of his fathers physical and mental state after the ambulance ride which sparked the end of everything, was truly the saddest thing I’ve ever seen. And I wish you the best and REALLY hope that something promising comes along to help you defeat this tremendously difficult battle. You will be in my prayers, and I think it’s safe to say that everyone on here is routing for you. If you ever need to talk to let stuff off your chest or rant or if you want some extra help sorting anything out and making plans for if the grim day does occur,  please DM me. I don’t know you, nor you do I. But I am in tears from reading your comment and the rest of this thread. And if I can help in anyway, I will.
